title: KutzInventory export 3.x
description: The JSON that tools/inventory_export.js --format 3 writes (export/inventory.json) and that the Companion uploads to cr0m. Version 3.x omits selected character-profile fields listed below. Since 3.0.0 there are no stats, sheet, talents, spec, role, reputation, PvP or achievement points, and equipped items are only slotId, id and link (3.0.0 to 3.13.0 also left out statistics). Money is in copper. Times are ISO-8601 UTC strings or null. Objects marked 'open' are copied from the game as-is and may gain keys in any 3.x release; readers must ignore keys they do not know. See schema/README.md for the versioning rules. 3.1.0 adds raids: the cr0m raids tracked with /kinv raid that recorded something. 3.2.0 adds observations: drop, quest and vendor events recorded while enabled (/kinv track; on by default for a new install since addon 1.13.0). Retained events export even after recording is turned off. 3.4.0 adds characters[].crafted: the items the character created, counted as they are made. 3.6.0: quest observations may carry text, the quest's own words as the game showed them. 3.7.0: loot observations may come from a corpse's group-loot roll list (src.via roll, src.threshold), name a boss's encounter (src.encounter), and mark the item the character won by roll (items[].won). Optional characters[].legacyTree added in inventory 2.1.0 / 3.8.0. 3.9.0: trainer observations (a class or profession trainer's list as the game showed it, with costs, spell ids and the trainer's reaction rx); vendor observations may carry rx and filtered. 3.10.0: observations may carry npcs, a cumulative per-install summary of the creatures the player looked at, with install naming the install it summarises. 3.11.0: taxi observations (a flight master's reachable nodes and prices) and flight observations (how long a flight between two nodes took); npcs entries may carry svc, the services an NPC was seen to offer; quest observations may carry lv, group, freq, timed and startItem (accept) and xp and rep (turnin: the reputation changes, never a standing). 3.12.0: gossip and quest-greeting text game-authored readable pages and NPC spoken lines. Quest accepts may carry objective definitions and points of interest on the player's acceptance map. 3.13.0: tame observations (a hunter's tamed beast and what its new pet showed) and credit observations (which creature, item or object counted for a quest objective). 3.14.0: characters[].statistics is exported again, with its updated.statistics stamp. 3.15.0 adds, all optional: observations.items, observations.kills (with killsInstall), npcs[].inst, suffix and bonus beside an observation item's link, characters[].statisticsDays, vendorDay / vendorLimited / vendors on a price, and characters[].questLog (the character's current quest log and objective progress).

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this format. A reader that knows 3.0 can read any 3.x.

prices.description: Every item a vendor sells or buys that the characters have seen, keyed by item ID. Vendor observations only.

updatedBy.description: Character key that last saw the warband bank.

raids.description: Since 3.1.0 (absent before). The cr0m raids tracked in game with /kinv raid <string> that recorded at least one event, oldest scheduled start first. Account-wide: every character of the uploaded file(s) recorded into these. The addon does not verify the signature; receiving servers must verify authorization independently.

open.description: Open: copied from the game, keys may change between client builds.

item.description: One item stack. id is required; the rest is copied from the game (open).

bag.description: Game bag ID (-1 keyring, 0-5 bags, 6-14 bank tabs, 15-23 warband tabs, guild tab number).

updated.description: Raw from the addon for bags/bank (usually null); ISO time for guild tabs.

vendorBuy.description: What the cheapest vendor seen charges per item.

vendorSell.description: What a vendor pays you per item (the game's sell price).

vendorDay.description: Since 3.15.0: the day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) the cheapest vendor was last seen selling it. Never a time of day. Absent when no vendor was seen or the saved file has no time for it.

vendorLimited.description: Since 3.15.0: the cheapest vendor's stock of it was limited when last seen. Absent otherwise.

vendors.description: Since 3.15.0: every vendor seen selling it (KutzInventory 1.21.0 keeps up to 9 per saved file; older saved files know only the cheapest), cheapest first, then by name. A vendor is known by its name; npc is there when the addon read its id.

name.description: The vendor's name (an NPC, never a player).

npc.description: The vendor's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never stored).

limited.description: Its stock of the item was limited when last seen.

day.description: The day (UTC) it was last seen selling it.

key.description: Stable character id, unique per export. An existing Name-Realm key stays with its GUID (or the first login for a legacy entry without a GUID). A different GUID uses Name-Surname-Realm, or Name-<guid tail>-Realm without a surname; further collisions append the GUID and, if needed, a number before the realm. Treat this as opaque; never reconstruct it from name and realm.

surname.description: Forever surname. Absent when the character has none.

guid.description: Stable game GUID. Personal identifier: do not show publicly.

recording.description: Optional. What the last save captured (written by exporters that record logout checkpoints).

location.description: Last good location. Exact coordinates: treat as private.

updated.description: Section name -> when it was last read. 3.x leaves out the sections it no longer exports (sheet, stats, talents, reputation, pvp). statistics is back since 3.14.0.

equipped.description: What the character wears, as of the last save: enough to show gear between Battle.net refreshes (the API has the rest as of logout). Closed: name, quality, stats and durability come from the API or the item catalog.

slotId.description: The game's inventory slot (GetInventorySlotInfo): 1 head ... 16 main hand, 17 off hand, 18 ranged.

link.description: The item link as the game gives it (enchant and suffix IDs are inside).

statistics.description: Since 3.14.0 (3.0.0 to 3.13.0 left it out; a reader must treat an absent list as not exported, not as empty). The Statistics tab of the achievement window: one entry per statistic with a value, { id, name, category, parent?, value }. Values are the game's own text or numbers and can include amounts of gold; consumers must apply their own access controls. Read after login, then after combat at most once per ten minutes.

hearth.description: Since 3.5.0: where the Hearthstone is set, the inn's town or district as the game names it (GetBindLocation), recorded by KutzInventory 1.11.0 or later. Absent until the game has said. Treat as private, like location.

statisticsDays.description: Since 3.15.0 (KutzInventory 1.21.0): the statistics whose value changed, per day, for the last 30 days, oldest day first. statistics stays the newest full list; this is the history a reader can draw a per-day line from. A day lists a statistic when a reading that day differed from the reading before it, with the value of the day's last reading. A first reading records no day. Values can include amounts of gold, like statistics; consumers must apply their own access controls.

id.description: The statistic's id, as in statistics[].id.

value.description: The game's own text or number, as in statistics[].value.

crafted.description: Since 3.4.0: the items this character created, counted at each of its own "You create" lines in the loot chat (profession crafts and things like conjured food alike), so an item made and then sold, mailed, used or disenchanted before the next save still counts. Always on from KutzInventory 1.10.0; crafts before `since` are unknown. Absent when nothing has been counted.

since.description: When counting began on this character (the first craft seen by KutzInventory 1.10.0 or later).

total.description: Items created since `since`. Not capped by `items` or `days`.

items.description: Per item, sorted by itemId. If there are more than 5000, the most recently made are kept.

name.description: The item's name from its link, in the client's language.

count.description: Items made (a craft that makes 5 adds 5).

crafts.description: How many times it was made ("You create" lines).

days.description: Items made per day, sorted by date: the newest 120 days on which something was made. The date is the player's local date.

string.description: The raid's string exactly as cr0m issued it: KR1.<CODE>.<instanceId>.<startUnix>.<sig>. CODE is the 6-character join code, instanceId 0 when unknown, startUnix the scheduled start in UTC seconds, sig cr0m's 12-character signature (the addon can't check it).

events.description: In time order. The addon records at most 2000 per raid; two saved files tracking the same raid are merged.

raidEvent.description: One thing the addon saw while the raid was active: from 2 h before its start to 8 h after, in a party or raid group, inside an instance. t is when (UTC). Optional fields are left out when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: Entered the instance (also after leaving it and coming back).

instanceId.description: The instance ID the client reports (GetInstanceInfo), which may differ from the string's (journal vs map IDs).

instanceName.description: The instance's name, in the client's language.

oneOf.description: Left the instance (or the raid's window ended, or the group broke up). t is when the loading screen out started.

encounterName.description: Its name, in the client's language.

groupSize.description: Group size the encounter was scaled to.

oneOf.description: ENCOUNTER_END: a kill (success) or a wipe.

encounterName.description: Its name, in the client's language.

oneOf.description: A loot line (CHAT_MSG_LOOT) for anyone in the group, including bonus rolls.

itemLink.description: The item link as the client printed it.

looter.description: The recording character's stable characters[].key for its own loot; other group members use Name-Realm, else the name as the loot line wrote it.

oneOf.description: The group's members, at each start and after each encounter_end.

members.description: Each member, sorted: the recording character's stable characters[].key, other members as Name-Realm.

observations.description: Since 3.2.0, only when drop tracking recorded something (absent otherwise, and in 3.0.0 / 3.1.0). The events drop tracking recorded (loot, quest, vendor and, since 3.9.0, trainer; since 3.11.0, taxi and flight) (/kinv track; opt-in until KutzInventory 1.13.0, on by default since, /kinv track drops off stops it), from the saved table KutzInventoryObsDB. Since 3.12.0 also game-authored gossip, quest greetings readable pages and lines spoken by identified NPCs. Since 3.13.0 also hunter tames and objective credit (which creature, item or object counted for a quest objective; never the progress numbers). Never the player's gold (no coin loot, no player money), player chat, mail or guild data; since 3.16.0 a quest event's rewards.money is the quest's listed money reward, a fact about the quest, not anyone's gold. Contains character identity and location history; consumers must apply their own access controls. Since 3.10.0 also npcs (with install): a cumulative per-install summary of the creatures the player looked at; a later export from the same install replaces it. Readers must ignore event types and fields they do not know. Since 3.15.0 also items (each item's own facts, read once per item and game build), kills (with killsInstall: creatures killed per day) and, on npcs, inst (creatures seen inside instances); events may be empty when any of them is present.

addon.description: The KutzInventory version that recorded it ("unknown" when the saved file did not say).

install.description: Since 3.10.0, with npcs: the install the npcs summary belongs to, the saved file's random prefix (the same one the event ids start with). When an export merges several saved files (several game accounts) that hold a summary, their prefixes sorted and joined by +. A summary replaces every earlier one whose install shares a part with it; it is not cryptographic or guaranteed globally unique.

events.description: Oldest first. At most 5000 and about 2 MB of JSON; the addon keeps 30 days. Empty only when the section carries npcs.

npcs.description: Since 3.10.0: the creatures this install's players looked at (target, mouseover, an open vendor / quest / trainer window, a loot corpse), one entry per NPC id, sorted by npc. Cumulative per install: a later export replaces an earlier one with the same install; counts are totals, not deltas. Only creatures no player controls, only outside instances. No GUIDs, no player names, no time finer than a day, no order of sightings. At most 3000 (the most recently seen) and about 1 MB of JSON.

items.description: Since 3.15.0: the items' own facts, sorted by id, at most 4000 (the most recently changed) and about 1.5 MB of JSON. The addon keeps what fits its saved-file budget (dropping the least recently met) and reads an item again when it is met after being dropped, so an export is not the whole history: a reader keeps what it was given before.

killsInstall.description: Since 3.15.0, with kills: the install ids whose counts kills adds up, joined by "+" (the same ids as install).

kills.description: Since 3.15.0: kills per day, sorted by day, npc and level, the last 30 days the addon kept. Cumulative per install: a later export from the same install replaces the counts of the days it lists (a day's count only grows).

observationWhere.description: Where it happened. Fields the client did not give are left out.

map.description: The map / instance ID: GetInstanceInfo() instanceID.

itype.description: Inside an instance only: GetInstanceInfo() instanceType (party, raid, scenario, pvp, arena, ...).

difficulty.description: Inside an instance only: GetInstanceInfo() difficultyID.

x.description: Outside instances only: map position 0-1, 4 decimal places.

y.description: Outside instances only: map position 0-1, 4 decimal places.

observationWho.description: The recording character's level, class ID and faction, because drops and vendors depend on them, and (since 3.3.0) its own name and surname so cr0m can credit the character that found something. Never anyone else's name, and no realm, guild or GUID.

name.description: Since 3.3.0: the recording character's own given name (UnitName("player")). Never another player's.

surname.description: Since 3.3.0: the recording character's own surname (Forever's GetUnitName adds it), when it has one.

observationLink.description: Since 3.3.0: the item's link cut down to its quality colour, id and name, e.g. |cffa335ee|Hitem:19019|h[Thunderfury, Blessed Blade]|h|r. The id is the item's own. Lets cr0m name an item no database has yet. The rest of the game's link (the player's level, spec, enchants) is never kept. A copy with a random suffix has the same link (the plain item's id); since 3.15.0 its suffix is said beside it, in suffix / bonus.

observationEvent.description: One recorded event. type picks the shape.

oneOf.description: A loot window was opened: one event per loot source in it. Every window counts as an open (a coins-only corpse has items []), so drops / opens is a rate. The same corpse or node opened twice is one event; skinning a corpse is a separate open of kind skin. Coins and currencies are never recorded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

kind.description: chest = any game object that isn't a herb or ore node; container = an item opened from the bags (src.item); quest = a quest reward container. disenchant (since 3.16.0): the window of the character's own Disenchant (within 5 s of the cast succeeding, one window per cast); src.item is the destroyed item and is always present (a window without it is not recorded), and nothing else is.

npc.description: The creature's NPC ID, from its GUID.

object.description: The game object's ID, from its GUID.

item.description: kind container: the opened item's ID. kind disenchant (since 3.16.0): the destroyed item's ID, from the window's item source GUID or else the bag item the cast was aimed at.

guid.description: Creatures and objects only, never a player, a player's pet or an item. Consumers may use it to deduplicate a kill across reports; server handling is outside this schema.

level.description: The creature's level when a unit showed it (the same NPC at two levels is two sources).

via.description: How the source was known: slot = GetLootSourceInfo, target = the dead target when the window opened (no GetLootSourceInfo). roll (since 3.7.0) = not a loot window but the corpse's group-loot roll list (Need / Greed), recorded also when another player opened the corpse: it holds only the items at or above threshold, never coins or anything below it, so it is a partial open. Items a loot window of the same character showed are not repeated in it. Without a guid the corpse was not known (kind other).

encounter.description: Since 3.7.0: the DungeonEncounter id of a boss killed while recording (ENCOUNTER_END), on that boss's loot.

threshold.description: Since 3.7.0, via roll only: the group's loot threshold quality (0 poor ... 4 epic) when the list was rolled; the list is every item of that quality or better.

items.description: The items in the window from this source (empty: nothing but coins, or nothing).

id.description: Item ID.

suffix.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's random suffix id, from its link ("of the Bear"). The item is still id: a suffixed copy is a variant of that one item, never an item of its own. Absent for a copy with no suffix id.

bonus.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's bonus ids, from its link, ascending. On the Forever client a random suffix is a bonus id (6560 with bonus [12729] is "Soldier's Shield of Intellect"). Same rule as suffix: one item, a variant.

won.description: Since 3.7.0: the recording character won this item by roll (its own "You won" loot line). Absent otherwise; who else won is never recorded.

oneOf.description: A quest was accepted or turned in. rewards on turnin; since 3.16.0 also on accept (the offer window's), with rewards.money the quest's own listed reward, never the player's money. text (since 3.6.0) is the quest's own words. Since 3.11.0: lv, group, freq, timed and startItem only on accept; xp and rep only on turnin; each is left out when the client did not say or the addon was not sure. Since 3.12.0: obj and poi only on accept.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The giver (accept) or ender (turnin), when it is a creature.

object.description: The giver or ender, when it is a game object.

rewards.description: The quest's reward as the quest window listed it to the recording character: on turnin the reward window (QUEST_COMPLETE); since 3.16.0 (KutzInventory 1.23.0) also on accept, from the offer window (QUEST_DETAIL), only when that window showed this very quest and listed something. A quest accepted without an offer window (shared, auto-accepted) has none. Each key since 3.16.0 is left out when the window did not list it or the client did not answer plainly: absent means not recorded, never none. choices is always there on a turnin and never on an accept.

id.description: Item ID.

suffix.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's random suffix id, from its link ("of the Bear"). The item is still id: a suffixed copy is a variant of that one item, never an item of its own. Absent for a copy with no suffix id.

bonus.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's bonus ids, from its link, ascending. On the Forever client a random suffix is a bonus id (6560 with bonus [12729] is "Soldier's Shield of Intellect"). Same rule as suffix: one item, a variant.

choose.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the choose-one item rewards (GetNumQuestChoices, GetQuestItemInfo / GetQuestItemLink "choice"), in the window's order, with their counts; the first 10. On a turnin choices still lists the same items' ids, for older readers.

id.description: Item ID.

suffix.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's random suffix id, from its link ("of the Bear"). The item is still id: a suffixed copy is a variant of that one item, never an item of its own. Absent for a copy with no suffix id.

bonus.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's bonus ids, from its link, ascending. On the Forever client a random suffix is a bonus id (6560 with bonus [12729] is "Soldier's Shield of Intellect"). Same rule as suffix: one item, a variant.

choices.description: Turnin only: the choice rewards' item IDs (the same items as choose, kept for older readers).

chose.description: Turnin only: the picked choice reward's item ID.

money.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the quest's money reward in copper as the window listed it (GetRewardMoney() with that quest's window open). A fact about the quest at this character's level, the same for every character of that level: never the player's money (GetMoney is never called) and never QUEST_TURNED_IN's money argument. At the level cap (see cap) it can include XP converted to money. Absent when 0 or unreadable.

xp.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the XP the window listed (GetRewardXP), under the same rules as a turnin's top-level xp (under the level cap, XP not turned off, never 0). On a turnin the top-level xp stays too.

spells.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the reward spell ids (C_QuestInfoSystem.GetQuestRewardSpells(quest)), ascending, each once; the lowest 8.

title.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the title the quest grants (GetRewardTitle), as the game named it.

cap.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the character was at the level cap when the window was read (UnitLevel("player") >= GetMaxPlayerLevel(), both known). Its money can then include converted XP, and xp is absent. Absent when under the cap or unknown. On its own it lists no reward.

skill.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: skill points the quest grants in one skill line (GetRewardSkillLineID, GetRewardSkillPoints). Only when both are known.

cur.description: Since 3.16.0, both acts: the reward currencies (C_QuestInfoSystem.GetQuestRewardCurrencies(quest): currencyID and totalRewardAmount), sorted by id, each id once; the lowest 8.

id.description: The currency id.

text.description: Since 3.6.0: the quest's text as the game showed it to the recording character, with that character's own name put back to $N. On accept: title, details, objectives. On turnin: title, progress, completion. Recorded once per quest and act while that event is kept, so most repeats carry none. Game text, nothing about the player.

details.description: The description in the window that offers the quest (GetQuestText).

progress.description: What the ender says before the quest is complete (GetProgressText).

completion.description: What the ender says in the reward window (GetRewardText).

lv.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest's level as the quest log shows it (C_QuestLog.GetInfo level). On a client that scales quests to the character, the level it showed this character.

group.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest log's suggested group size (suggestedGroup), only when 2 or more.

freq.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: a daily or weekly quest (the quest log's frequency, Enum.QuestFrequency Daily or Weekly). Absent for any other quest, or when the client did not say.

timed.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest has a time limit (C_QuestLog.GetTimeAllowed above 0 when it was accepted). Absent when it has none or the client did not say: absent is not proof of no timer.

startItem.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the item that started the quest (the QUEST_DETAIL questStartItemID), only when the window that offered it showed this very quest.

xp.description: Since 3.11.0, turnin only: the XP the reward window showed (GetRewardXP), as offered to this character (it may include the character's XP bonuses). Only while the character is under the level cap with XP not turned off; never 0.

rep.description: Since 3.11.0, turnin only: the reputation the turn-in changed, as changes, never a standing. Each faction's standing was read when the reward window opened and again about a second after the turn-in; only factions in both reads that changed, sorted by f, each once. What this character received, not the quest's listed reward: with its reputation bonuses and any spill-over to other factions, so the same quest can differ between characters. The Guild faction (1168) and renown factions are left out. Absent when nothing changed, more than 6 changed, or something else could have moved them in between (loot, combat, another reward window or turn-in, more than 5 minutes from the window to the turn-in).

d.description: The change in reputation points this character received (with its reputation bonuses): positive gained, negative lost. Never 0.

obj.description: Quest objective definitions in quest-log order. Player progress and completion status are excluded.

rows.description: Since 3.13.0 (KutzInventory 1.20.0), accept only and only beside obj: how many objectives C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives listed when obj was read, unusable rows included (never fewer than obj's length). obj keeps the client's order but skips unusable rows and stops at 12, so obj[k] is the client's k-th objective exactly when obj's length equals rows. Absent on older events and when the client listed more than 40.

poi.description: Distinct GetQuestsOnMap markers for the acceptance UI map. The exporter rounds x and y to two decimal places of map percent.

oneOf.description: A vendor window was opened: what was for sale at that moment (not proof of the vendor's full or future stock). Since 3.9.0 read under the window's all-items filter (put back at once); prices are as shown, after any reputation discount (see rx).

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

rx.description: Since 3.9.0: the NPC's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Prices and costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount; rx lets a reader tell a list price from a discounted one. Absent when the client did not say.

filtered.description: Since 3.9.0: the merchant window's item filter (this class only) could not be switched to all for the read, so items it hides are missing from this list. Absent when the list was read unfiltered (or the client has no such filter).

id.description: Item ID.

suffix.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's random suffix id, from its link ("of the Bear"). The item is still id: a suffixed copy is a variant of that one item, never an item of its own. Absent for a copy with no suffix id.

bonus.description: Since 3.15.0: this copy's bonus ids, from its link, ascending. On the Forever client a random suffix is a bonus id (6560 with bonus [12729] is "Soldier's Shield of Intellect"). Same rule as suffix: one item, a variant.

price.description: Copper per n, as the vendor shows it (0 when it costs only items or currencies).

cost.description: Item or currency costs per purchase.

limited.description: The vendor's limited stock, or null when unlimited.

oneOf.description: Since 3.9.0: a class or profession trainer's window was opened: every service it lists (all three type filters were switched on for the read and put back after), as this character saw them. The hunter's Beast Training window is never recorded. The same trainer with the same list (st aside) and rx is recorded at most once in 7 days. Costs are game prices, not the player's money.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The trainer's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

kind.description: profession: C_Trainer.GetTrainerType() is Tradeskills; class: any other trainer but Pet (class trainers, weapon masters and other general trainers).

rx.description: Since 3.9.0: the NPC's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Prices and costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount; rx lets a reader tell a list price from a discounted one. Absent when the client did not say.

rows.description: The services in the order the window lists them, headers left out. At most 400.

s.description: The spell ID, from C_TooltipInfo.GetTrainerService (the client has no GetTrainerServiceSpellID). Absent when the client gave none.

name.description: The service's name (GetTrainerServiceInfo), at most 120 bytes.

rank.description: Its sub text, e.g. Rank 4 (profession trainers: Apprentice, Journeyman ...).

lv.description: The character level it needs; absent when none.

skill.description: The skill it needs (GetTrainerServiceSkillReq), e.g. Blacksmithing.

needs.description: Abilities it needs first (GetTrainerServiceAbilityReq), at most 5.

cost.description: Copper, as the trainer shows it to this character (after any reputation discount; see rx). A game price, not the player's money.

st.description: a = available (can be learned now), u = unavailable (not yet), k = known. Not part of the 7-day check.

oneOf.description: Since 3.11.0: a flight master's map was opened (TAXIMAP_OPENED): every node this character can fly to from the flight master's own node, with its price. Node ids come from C_TaxiMap.GetAllTaxiNodes, joined by slot to the window's own slot functions; when the client gives no node ids, the two disagree, there is not exactly one current node, or more than 200 nodes are reachable, nothing is recorded. The same flight master, node, list of nodes and prices and rx is recorded at most once in 7 days. Costs are game prices, not the player's money. No node names, no GUID.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The flight master's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

node.description: The flight master's own node: the taxi node id (TaxiNodes) the window marks as current.

rx.description: The flight master's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount. Absent when the client did not say.

to.description: Every node reachable from node (the window's REACHABLE nodes), sorted by node, each once and never node itself. Nodes the character has not discovered or cannot reach are not listed. Empty when none is reachable yet.

cost.description: Copper, TaxiNodeCost as the window shows it to this character. A game price, not the player's money.

hops.description: How many flight legs the route takes (GetNumRoutes). Absent when the client gave none.

oneOf.description: Since 3.11.0: a flight this character took, from boarding to landing. Started by TakeTaxiNode in a taxi window that was read (the destination), PLAYER_CONTROL_LOST and UnitOnTaxi true; ended by PLAYER_CONTROL_GAINED with UnitOnTaxi false. Recorded only when the landing is known to be at to: the position on the taxi map is by that node (no other node closer), or, when the position could not be read, the next taxi window within 2 minutes is at to. Once per from and to in 30 days. No where: never a position or route trail.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When the flight landed, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

from.description: The taxi node id the flight started at (the flight master's own node).

to.description: The taxi node id it landed at, the one chosen in the window. Never the same as from.

sec.description: Seconds from boarding to landing (GetTime, rounded), as this character flew it. Flights under 5 seconds or over an hour are not recorded.

oneOf.description: Game-authored gossip or quest greeting; exactly one subject. Gossip options and GUIDs are excluded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: One page of game-authored readable text. A source ID is optional; mail and authored letters are excluded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

item.description: Optional bag item ID supported by the format. Addon 1.19.0 does not record bag items.

object.description: World game object ID. Addon 1.19.0 requires this source to record a page.

oneOf.description: Sanitized game dialogue or emote from an identified creature. No speaker GUID or recipient.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

text.description: ASCII game dialogue. The addon normalizes curly quotes, en and em dashes, and ellipses before checking the text.

oneOf.description: Since 3.13.0: a hunter tamed a beast. npc, lv and fam are the target's when Tame Beast began; the new pet bore the target's name (and its level and creature id wherever readable), so a cast that went to another unit is not recorded. spells, spd and diet are what the new pet showed within 60 s. where is where the tame began. Never the pet's GUID or name, nor the target's name.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The tamed creature's NPC id, from the target's GUID when Tame Beast began. Never guessed: a tame without it is not recorded.

lv.description: The creature's level (UnitLevel on the target when the tame began). Absent for a skull or when unreadable.

fam.description: UnitCreatureFamily on the target: the client's family id (the stable value; prefer it), else its name in the client's language (up to 40; see loc). The new pet had the same family wherever both were read.

spells.description: The new pet's spellbook as the client listed it (C_SpellBook pet bank, else GetSpellBookItemName(i, "pet")), sorted by s, each spell id once; the same in two reads in a row. Only entries whose id names the spell the book shows; commands such as Attack are left out. Absent means not read: the book listed nothing, or never the same twice, within 60 s of the tame (or the client has no timer); it does not mean the beast has no abilities.

rank.description: The book's subtext ("Rank 2"), when it shows one.

spd.description: The new pet's main-hand attack speed in hundredths of a second (UnitAttackSpeed("pet")), read with the pet alive and neither it nor the player in combat, within 60 s of the tame. Without spdAura the pet had no aura at that read.

spdAura.description: Only with spd: the pet had at least one aura at every read, so spd may include a haste or slow effect.

diet.description: The new pet's diet as the client names it (C_PetInfo.GetPetFoodTypes), sorted: display labels in the client's language (see loc), not ids.

loc.description: Since 3.13.0: GetLocale() when the tame was recorded, e.g. enUS: the language of a fam name and of diet. Use those labels only for a locale you know. Absent when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: Since 3.13.0: an objective of a quest in the log counted something. When the objective's numFulfilled rose (read in memory to see the rise; never saved or exported) and the player's own evidence of the 6 s before named exactly one cause: a creature that died untapped by others, an item from the player's own loot line, an object whose window (gossip, greeting, quest, page) the player opened. Once per quest, objective and id per install. Never the progress numbers or anything about another player.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

i.description: The objective's position in C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives(quest), from 1 (only the first 12 are compared). See rows for when it lines up with the accept event's obj.

rows.description: How many objectives C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives listed for the quest when the credit was read (at least i). The addon writes it on every credit; absent only on events from development builds before it. i refers to the accept event's obj[i] (counting from 1) only when that accept's obj length equals its rows and equals this rows.

ot.description: The objective's type as the client gave it. monster carries npc, item carries item, object carries object.

npc.description: ot monster: the creature id, from the dead creature's GUID.

item.description: ot item: the item id, from the player's own loot line.

object.description: ot object: the object id, from the GUID of the object whose window the player opened.

by.description: How the cause was told. name: the only candidate named as whole words in the objective's text (for an item, its bag count also agreed whenever the client gave one). sole (ot monster only): the only creature that died in the window, while the player was not grouped and had no pet out for the window. Items and objects are told by name only. Treat sole as the weaker.

oneOf.description: Since 3.16.0: the reputation one kill gave this character. From the client's own "Reputation with %s increased by %d." (or decreased) line, tied to a creature only when every creature this player saw die untapped by others, from 2 s before the line to 1 s after it, had the same NPC id; nothing within 5 s of a quest turn-in or while a reward window was open. The faction's id comes from the character's reputation list by its name (a name two factions share records nothing). Never a standing, never the creature's GUID. Once per npc, lv, f and d per install.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The creature's NPC id, from the dead creature's GUID (the GUID is never kept).

lv.description: The creature's level, when every death tied to the line showed the same plain level. Absent for a skull, when unreadable, or when they differed.

f.description: The faction id (C_Reputation factionID), found by the faction's name in this character's reputation list.

d.description: The change this character received, as the line gave it: positive for increased, negative for decreased. Includes this character's own reputation bonuses, like a turn-in's rep.d; who.level tells a reduced amount from a full one.

legacyTree.description: Current character Legacy trait ranks and choice entries as applied (changes staged before Apply Changes are not recorded), read without loading Blizzard_LegacySystem. Optional until all three trees are available.

questLog.description: Since 3.15.0 (KutzInventory 1.21.0). Snapshot of the character's current quest log in log order, read from C_QuestLog.GetNumQuestLogEntries, C_QuestLog.GetInfo and C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives (with legacy GetNumQuestLogEntries, GetQuestLogTitle, GetNumQuestLeaderBoards and GetQuestLogLeaderBoard fallbacks). Absent when not recorded (old addon or unavailable API); quests: [] means recorded and empty. Treat as private character activity.

at.description: Unix seconds (time()) when the quest log was read.

quests.description: Quests in quest log order, at most 35 entries. Empty array when the character currently has no quests in the log.

id.description: Quest ID (C_QuestLog.GetInfo.questID, else GetQuestLogTitle).

title.description: Quest title as shown in the quest log (C_QuestLog.GetInfo.title, else GetQuestLogTitle), with UI markup removed.

lv.description: Quest level as the log shows it (C_QuestLog.GetInfo.level, else GetQuestLogTitle).

header.description: Zone or category header the quest sits under in the quest log (the preceding isHeader row's title), with UI markup removed.

done.description: Complete and ready to turn in (C_QuestLog.IsComplete / C_QuestLog.ReadyForTurnIn, else GetQuestLogTitle isComplete == 1). Absent otherwise.

failed.description: Failed, for example when a timer ran out (C_QuestLog.IsFailed, else GetQuestLogTitle isComplete == -1). Absent otherwise.

obj.description: Quest objectives in client order, at most 12 (C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives, else GetNumQuestLeaderBoards and GetQuestLogLeaderBoard). Empty array for quests with no objectives.

text.description: Objective text as the client shows it (for example "Kobold Vermin slain: 3/10"), with UI markup removed.

have.description: Progress fulfilled so far (C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives numFulfilled). Absent when the API does not provide it.

need.description: Required progress count (C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives numRequired). Absent when the API does not provide it.

done.description: Whether the objective is finished (C_QuestLog.GetQuestObjectives finished, else GetQuestLogLeaderBoard isCompleted).

type.description: Objective type as the client reports it (for example "monster", "item", "object", "event").

observationNpc.description: Since 3.10.0: what the client showed about one creature, summed over this install's sightings. Fields the client did not give (or kept secret) are left out.

npc.description: The NPC ID, from the creature's GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

name.description: The creature's name as last seen (UnitName), in the client's language, under the subtitle's rules: never an owner title, anything with an apostrophe-s, the recording character's name, markup or a GUID shape.

lv.description: [min, max] of UnitLevel over the sightings (min <= max). A skull (-1) is never a level.

boss.description: UnitLevel was -1 (a skull) while the creature was a world boss or the player was at the level cap. A skull seen by a lower character is not kept.

ct.description: UnitCreatureType: the client's creature type id (1 Beast, 7 Humanoid, ...), else its localized name (up to 40). Companions (12, Non-combat Pet) are never recorded.

fam.description: UnitCreatureFamily: the client's family id, else its localized name (up to 40). Absent for creatures without a family.

rxA.description: UnitReaction(unit, "player") as last seen by an Alliance character, read only while it was alive and out of combat: 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly .. 8 exalted.

rxH.description: UnitReaction(unit, "player") as last seen by a Horde character, read only while it was alive and out of combat: 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly .. 8 exalted.

sub.description: The subtitle under its name ("Journeyman Tailor"), from the unit tooltip, only when the tooltip's lines prove it is one (line 1 the unit's name, line 3 the level line, line 2 not); never an owner title ("X's Pet") or anything with an apostrophe-s.

svc.description: Since 3.11.0: the services this NPC was seen to offer, sorted, each once: vendor (a merchant window), repair (that window could repair: CanMerchantRepair), flight (a flight master map), trainer, bank, guildbank, inn (CONFIRM_BINDER or HEARTHSTONE_BOUND while talking to it), auction, stable, battlemaster, spirit (a spirit healer), guild (guild registrar or charter seller), tabard. From PLAYER_INTERACTION_MANAGER_FRAME_SHOW (Enum.PlayerInteractionType, by name) and the windows the addon reads; each counts as a near sighting. A set summed over sightings, never gossip text.

spd.description: Beasts only: main-hand attack speed in hundredths of a second (UnitAttackSpeed), read alive and out of combat; the value seen most often (a tie keeps the one seen first).

hp.description: Since 3.16.0: the creature's maximum health (UnitHealthMax), one entry per level (and diff inside an instance), sorted by lv then diff; at most 6 levels, the most recently seen. Read at a sighting (at most once per creature per 30 s), only alive and at a plain level of 1 or more; v is the value seen most often of up to 4 distinct readings. A buff or debuff on the creature can change it, so a reader should want two installs to agree before showing it.

diff.description: The instance difficulty id (GetInstanceInfo), present exactly when the value was read inside an instance; absent outside.

pw.description: Since 3.16.0: the creature's power (UnitPowerType and UnitPowerMax), one entry per level (and diff inside an instance), sorted by lv then diff; at most 6 levels, the most recently seen. Read as hp is; absent for a creature whose maximum was 0. t and v are the pair seen most often.

diff.description: The instance difficulty id (GetInstanceInfo), present exactly when the value was read inside an instance; absent outside.

day.description: The last day it was seen: whole days since 1970-01-01 (UTC), floor(unix time / 86400). Never a time of day.

cells.description: Where the player stood while within about 10 yards of it (CheckInteractDistance) or with a window open with it, so the player's position stands for the creature's: unordered counts of 1% map squares, sorted by uiMap, cx, cy. At most one count per square per 10 minutes in a session; the 40 most counted squares.

inst.description: Since 3.15.0 (KutzInventory 1.21.0): the instances it was seen in, [[instance map, difficulty, n]], sorted by map then difficulty; the 8 most counted. Inside an instance the client gives no position, so a creature seen only there has inst and no cells. At most one count per instance per 10 minutes in a session.

prefixItems.description: The instance's map ID: GetInstanceInfo() instanceID

observationLabel.description: Since 3.9.0: a short game label (a spell, rank, skill or ability name) as the game showed it. No UI markup (|), no control characters, and nothing shaped like a GUID.

recordedProse.description: Game prose with line breaks, without UI markup, GUID-shaped strings or other control characters.

observationItem.description: Since 3.15.0 (KutzInventory 1.21.0): what the game itself says about one item, read once per item and game build from a link made of the item id alone (never from a character's copy: no enchant, gems, maker or unique id), and read again when the build changes. The addon reads every item the player meets (bags, bank, gear, loot, vendor stock, quest rewards), a few a second, never in combat. The tooltip is the one the client showed the reading character with what is that character's own taken out (see tip).

id.description: Item ID. One entry per item: random suffixes are variants of it, never entries of their own.

day.description: The last day the entry's content changed (first read, a changed field or build, or a new or changed variant): whole days since 1970-01-01 (UTC). Never a time of day. Meeting the item again with nothing new leaves day unchanged.

build.description: The game build the facts were read on (GetBuildInfo version and build, "1.60.1.71037").

name.description: The item's name (GetItemInfo), without a suffix.

bind.description: GetItemInfo bindType: 0 none, 1 on pickup, 2 on equip, 3 on use, 4 quest.

set.description: Item set ID, when it belongs to a set.

slot.description: Equip location (INVTYPE_SHIELD), when it can be worn.

durability.description: Maximum durability, from the tooltip's "Durability n / m" line (the line itself is left out of tip).

stats.description: GetItemStats for the link: the client's stat key (ITEM_MOD_STAMINA_SHORT, RESISTANCE0_NAME for armor ...) -> the number, two decimal places at most.

tip.description: The tooltip's lines, top to bottom, after the cleaner in tools/tooltip_clean.js: a line is its left text, or [left, right] when it has a right text ("Off Hand" / "Shield"). English client. Taken out: colour codes and other markup (red only says the reading character does not meet a requirement), the durability line, set-piece counts ("(2/8)" becomes "(8)"), "Already known", cooldowns, maker or giver lines, "Equipment Sets: ..." and the appearance-collection line. Lines such as "Requires Level 40" or "Classes: Mage" are the item's own and stay.

variants.description: The random suffixes of this item that were met, sorted by suffix then bonus ids. They belong to this one item: a reader must never make an item out of a variant.

suffix.description: The link's suffix id (not used on the Forever client, whose suffixes are bonus ids).

name.description: The copy's full name as its link showed it ("Soldier's Shield of Intellect").

stats.description: GetItemStats for the suffixed link, when the client answered with numbers that differ from the plain item's (absent: not known, never "the same").

observationKill.description: Since 3.15.0 (KutzInventory 1.21.0): how many of one creature died to the player's group on one day. Counted when a creature dies in front of the player while the player is fighting and no other player has tapped it, whether or not anyone loots it. One number per day, creature and level: no corpse GUID, no time of day, nothing about any player.

npc.description: The creature's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never stored).

lv.description: Its level (UnitLevel). Absent when the client gave none (a skull).

legacyChallenges.description: Since 3.16.0 (KutzInventory 1.23.0). This character's view of the Legacy challenge achievements, read from GetAchievementInfo, GetAchievementNumCriteria and GetAchievementCriteriaInfo after login, after ACHIEVEMENT_EARNED / CRITERIA_EARNED / CRITERIA_UPDATE (at most one read per 30 s, never in combat), on /kinv scan and at a pre-logout checkpoint when a read is waiting. Saved only when something changed. Absent when not recorded (old addon, a client without the achievement functions, or no achievement answered). Format 2 never carries it. Private: earnedBy names another of the owner's characters.

at.description: Unix seconds (time()) of the last read that changed the content (also updated.legacyChallenges).

list.description: Sorted by id, ids unique. Set 60: every Legacy challenge (65 ids, from the legacy-challenges dataset of build 1.60.1.70938) the client knows. Set 61: ids 63969-64033, only those completed or with a criterion whose quantity is above 0.

id.description: Achievement ID.

set.description: 60: the Legacy challenges; 61: the second set (ids 63969-64033).

completed.description: GetAchievementInfo return 4: completed on this account as this character's client reports it.

wasEarnedByMe.description: GetAchievementInfo return 13, when a plain boolean: this character earned it.

earnedBy.description: GetAchievementInfo return 14, when a non-empty string: the name of the owner's character that earned it. Private: never show it to anyone but the owner.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD the client gives for completion (GetAchievementInfo returns 5-7: month, day, years since 2000). Only when completed and a real date.

criteria.description: GetAchievementCriteriaInfo for each of GetAchievementNumCriteria's criteria (at most 40), in the client's order; a criterion without its id or completion is left out.

id.description: Criteria ID (return 10).

quantity.description: Return 4: progress so far, when a whole number of 0 or more.

reqQuantity.description: Return 5: the progress needed, when a whole number of 0 or more.
